summary: Research free, commercially usable 3D assets and textures for a realistic Japanese-city extraction shooter: licence terms per source, concrete finds per need, each licence claim verified

sources.source: Poly Haven (polyhaven.com) - HDRIs, PBR textures and 3D models, all CC0. Read on 2026-11-12 from polyhaven.com/license, polyhaven.com/our-api, the public JSON API at api.polyhaven.com, and the CC0 deed at creativecommons.org.
sources.licence_summary:
Yes: every Poly Haven asset (HDRI, texture, model) is CC0, so it may be used, modified and shipped inside a commercially sold game, in any engine including Godot, with no credit required and no fee or revenue share. Redistribution is allowed too, so committing the files to the game repository and shipping them in the game build is fine. There is no engine restriction and no per-item licence variation: one licence covers the whole library. Credit is optional (they ask commercial users to consider supporting them on Patreon, which is a request, not a condition).

Library size today (from their API): 869 textures, 521 models, plus HDRIs.

What suits this game:
- Ground / park: terrain 131, rock 125, sand 60, gravel 13, bark 24 (useful for tree trunks), snow 8, plus aerial ground sets (30).
- City: concrete 80, plaster-concrete 136, brick 108, road 36, asphalt 20 (e.g. asphalt_01/03/05/06/07, clean_asphalt, worn_asphalt, road_damaged, road_damaged_2, asphalt_pit_lane), cobblestone 38, roofing 23, tiles 14.
- Metal: only 25, and almost all are rusty sheets, corrugated iron, shutters and container sides. Good for port, containers, shutters, fences; NOT suitable as gun finishes (no parkerised/anodised/blued steel or polymer). Gun materials need another source (e.g. ambientCG) or hand-authored PBR.
- Models: props 176, industrial 97, nature 110, plants 57, rocks 37, ground cover 32, structures 26, trees 20, buildings 13, grass 4, weapons 3 (firearms 2).
- Trees: only 20 entries and they are South African or conifer: pine/fir (pine_forest collection), jacaranda, island trees, quiver trees, Karoo shrubs, stumps and dead trunks. No Japanese species (no cherry, maple, ginkgo, zelkova, bamboo, cedar). Useful picks for a Japanese park are limited to stumps, dead trunks, roots, moss_01, fern_02, shrub_01-04, nettle, dandelion, celandine, periwinkle, weed_plant_02, grass_medium_02, and possibly the pines.
- Firearms: just two, both vintage (bolt_action_rifle_7_62, about 20k triangles; service_pistol, about 27.5k triangles). They do not match the game's existing gun list; only useful as world props or as a reference for worn-metal texturing.
- HDRIs: outdoor skies including 'pure sky' versions, useful for sky lighting.

Resolutions and sizes (measured from the API file listings):
- Textures: 1k, 2k, 4k, 8k (some scans up to 16k), each map as JPG, PNG or EXR. Example asphalt_02: diffuse JPG 0.73 MB at 1k, 3.08 MB at 2k, 11.65 MB at 4k, 38.8 MB at 8k; normal JPG 1.24 / 4.94 / 17.4 / 63 MB; combined AO-rough-metal 'arm' JPG 0.30 / 1.30 / 5.2 / 19.8 MB. A full 2k JPG set is roughly 10 MB; a 1k set roughly 2.5 MB. PNG is about 3x larger. Normal maps come in OpenGL form (nor_gl), which is what Godot expects, and the 'arm' packed map plugs straight into Godot ORM materials.
- HDRIs: 1k to 16k, .hdr and .exr. Example sky: .hdr 1.4 MB at 1k, 5.5 MB at 2k, 20.7 MB at 4k, 75 MB at 8k, 262 MB at 16k. 2k-4k .hdr is the sensible range.
- Models: blend, glTF, FBX, USD, with textures at 1k-8k. Small props are light: shrub_02 glTF totals about 2 MB at 1k and 4.8 MB at 2k; service_pistol glTF about 9.4 MB at 2k.

sources.risks:
Licence risk is about as low as it gets; the traps are practical, not legal.

1. Trees and big plants are far too heavy as downloaded. Triangle counts: jacaranda_tree 312k, tree_small_02 4.65 million, island_tree_01 3.7 million, fir_tree_01 7.85 million, pine_tree_01 17.4 million, grass_medium_02 1.04 million, celandine_01 1.75 million. These are film/offline-render assets (many are tagged 'geometry nodes', a Blender-only feature). They would need heavy reduction and hand-made LODs in Blender before use in an 8 GB game.
2. The repository's 100 MB single-file limit is broken by tree downloads: jacaranda_tree's glTF .bin is 208 MB and its FBX 132 MB, even at 1k textures. Do not commit these raw.
3. The API has a 'lods' flag on many models, but the file listings I opened showed no separate LOD files in the glTF/FBX downloads; LODs may exist only inside the .blend. Assume no ready-made game LODs.
4. Species mismatch: vegetation is South African (Karoo, quiver trees, jacaranda) and European-style conifers. Nothing is recognisably Japanese, so the library cannot dress a Tokyo park on its own.
5. Gun materials: the metal category will not give realistic firearm finishes. The two gun models are vintage and are not any of the game's weapons.
6. Trademarks/patents are not covered by CC0. Poly Haven models are generally unbranded, but check any prop for visible logos or real brand markings before shipping.
7. No warranty: CC0 comes with no guarantee of clearance. Poly Haven states assets are original work by its staff or contributing artists, which makes this a low risk.
8. Site vs assets: the CC0 grant covers the assets only. Preview renders, logos and site text are protected, and the site terms prohibit scraping without permission. Use the official API (free, commercial use allowed, needs a unique User-Agent header, and the API page asks that tools pulling live from it make the Poly Haven origin clear to users) or manual downloads. A one-off download of chosen assets for the game is ordinary use.
9. Memory: default download buttons often offer 4k/8k. Pick 1k-2k JPG deliberately; an 8k PNG set is 100+ MB per map and would blow both the memory budget and the 100 MB file limit.
10. Terms can change for future uploads, but CC0 is irrevocable for anything already obtained under it. Keep a note of the download date and asset page URL for each asset used.
11. AI training: the licence page sets no restriction on the assets themselves; nothing relevant to shipping a game.
sources.how_to_filter:
No licence filtering is needed: everything on the site is CC0.

To browse by category (website): https://polyhaven.com/textures/asphalt, /textures/concrete, /textures/road, /textures/terrain, /textures/bark, /textures/metal, /textures/rock; https://polyhaven.com/models/trees, /models/plants, /models/ground%20cover, /models/rocks, /models/industrial, /models/props, /models/buildings; https://polyhaven.com/hdris/outdoor (and the skies/pure-sky listings). An asset page is https://polyhaven.com/a/<asset_id>, e.g. https://polyhaven.com/a/rusty_metal_04.

On each asset page choose resolution 1K or 2K and format JPG (textures) or glTF/FBX (models) before downloading; for HDRIs choose 2K or 4K .hdr.

Machine-readable (no key, send a unique User-Agent):
- https://api.polyhaven.com/categories/textures and /categories/models for category counts
- https://api.polyhaven.com/assets?t=textures&c=asphalt (t = hdris | textures | models, c = category) returns ids, tags, polycount, max resolution
- https://api.polyhaven.com/files/<asset_id> lists every file with exact byte size and URL, so triangle count and file size can be checked BEFORE downloading. Rule of thumb for this game: reject any model whose polycount is above roughly 100k or whose .bin/.fbx is over 100 MB unless it will be reduced in Blender first.
sources.account_needed: None. No account, login or API key is needed to browse or download from the site or the default API endpoints. No terms had to be accepted and nothing was downloaded during this research.
sources.quality_for_this_game:
Textures and HDRIs: excellent fit. Photoscanned, physically based, realistic, and available at 1k-2k JPG at a few MB per set, which suits the 8 GB budget. Strongest uses: asphalt and damaged-road sets for streets, concrete/plaster/brick for the generated mid-rise buildings, terrain/rock/gravel/bark for the park, rusty and corrugated metal for the later port and airport service areas, and pure-sky HDRIs for lighting.

Models: mixed. Small props (industrial items, tools, containers, furniture, rocks, stumps, roots, small shrubs, ferns, weeds) are realistic and mostly light enough to use at 1k-2k with little work. Trees and dense vegetation are hero-quality to look at but unusable as shipped: millions of triangles, 100-200+ MB geometry files, no ready game LODs, and the wrong species for Japan. Treat them as raw material for a Blender reduction pass, not drop-in assets.

Weapons: effectively nothing for this game. Two vintage guns that do not match the roster, and no clean gun-finish metal textures.

Buildings: only 13 entries, mostly small structures/sheds from themed collections, not Japanese city architecture; the texture library is the useful part for buildings.

Overall: best single source for ground, road, concrete and sky; weak for Japanese vegetation, guns and buildings as models.

sources.source: ambientCG (ambientcg.com) - checked live on 2026-11-12 via its own licence page, homepage, an asset page and its public API
sources.licence_summary: Yes, usable. Every ambientCG asset is released under Creative Commons CC0 1.0 (public-domain dedication). That allows use in a commercially sold game, modification, and shipping the raw texture files inside the game build. There is no engine restriction of any kind, so Godot is fine. Credit is NOT required; the author says he would appreciate it and suggests the wording "Created using <asset name> from ambientCG.com, licensed under the Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal License." The licence is site-wide, not per item: I found no per-asset licence variations, and the licence page says it covers both the downloadable files and the preview renders. The CC0 waiver is written as not revocable, so files downloaded today stay CC0 even if the site later changes its terms.

sources.risks:
Low-risk source; the traps are practical rather than legal.

1. No warranty and no third-party clearance. CC0 waives only the author's own copyright. It does not waive trademarks, and the author does not promise that nothing in a photo belongs to someone else. Practical rule: avoid any material, decal or atlas that shows a readable brand, logo, sign or a recognisable artwork. The atlas/decal category includes graffiti sets (e.g. GraffitiSet001); graffiti is someone else's artwork photographed, so treat those as the one category to skip or check individually.
2. Do not use the ambientCG logo or name in a way that suggests endorsement. A plain credits line is fine.
3. No AI-training clause, no engine clause, no revenue cap and no separate terms-of-use page were found; the only legal pages are the licence page and a German imprint/privacy page. Nothing to accept.
4. Change of terms: the CC0 waiver is not revocable for files already released. Keep a small record per downloaded asset (asset ID, date, licence page URL) so the provenance is provable later.
5. Size trap for this repository: 4K and above break the 100 MB single-file limit as zips (4K-JPG 80-140 MB, 8K 300-600 MB, PNG 8K about 1 GB) and are too heavy for an 8 GB card. Use 1K-JPG (about 7-10 MB per zip) or 2K-JPG (about 24-36 MB per zip); commit the unpacked maps, not the zip. Terrain OBJ files are 118 MB at the smallest setting and cannot be committed.
6. Normal map direction: packs normally carry both an OpenGL and a DirectX normal map; Godot needs the OpenGL one. Picking the wrong one makes lighting look inverted. (File naming not re-verified today, see unverified.)
7. JPG colour maps are lossy; fine for ground and walls, but roughness/normal maps show less banding from the PNG pack if a surface is seen very close (weapon materials).
8. The site shows ads and has an optional Patreon supporter login; neither changes the licence.
sources.account_needed: No account needed to download. The only login on the site is an optional "Supporter Login" for Patreon backers (ad-free browsing, early access, bulk Nextcloud access). No terms to accept, no API key for the public API.
sources.how_to_filter:
No licence filter is needed: everything on the site is CC0. Filter only by type and keyword.

Website list pages (type values are comma-separated; sort options are Popular, Latest, Downloads, Oldest, Random, Alphabet):
- PBR surfaces: https://ambientcg.com/list?type=material,atlas,decal
- HDRI skies: https://ambientcg.com/list?type=hdri,hdri-element
- Models and terrains: https://ambientcg.com/list?type=3d-model,terrain
- Single asset page: https://ambientcg.com/view?id=Asphalt031

Public API (no key; better for the AI doing integration, because it returns exact file sizes):
- https://ambientcg.com/api/v2/full_json?type=Material&q=asphalt&limit=20&include=downloadData
- type accepts Material, HDRI, Atlas, Decal, Terrain (comma-separated); q is the keyword; numberOfResults gives the count.
- In the result pick the download attribute "1K-JPG" or "2K-JPG" and ignore 4K and above.
- The value type=3DModel did not filter (it returned the whole catalogue), so the correct API name for models is unconfirmed; use the website list page for models.

Asset ID families worth searching for this game: Asphalt, Road (with painted lines), Concrete, PavingStones, Tiles, Bricks, Metal, Planks/Wood, Bark, Ground, Fabric, LeafSet (foliage atlases), DaySkyHDRI / DayEnvironmentHDRI.
sources.quality_for_this_game:
Strong fit for surfaces, weak fit for objects.

Good for:
- Streets and park hardscape: asphalt, roads, concrete, paving stones, tiles, bricks. 79 results for "asphalt" alone. Most are photo-scanned (photogrammetry), so they read as real, not stylised; recent ones date from 2024 onward.
- Building facades and interiors: concrete, tiles, metal, wood/planks, fabric (there are collections such as "Kitchen" with 116 items and "Industrial Manufacturing Facility" with 110).
- Gun materials: the metal, plastic-like and fabric materials can serve as base layers for the seven rebuilt guns, but they are generic tiling surfaces, not weapon-specific wear textures. Expect them to give a correct base metal/polymer look; edge wear and markings still have to be made separately.
- Park vegetation: 30 leaf atlases (maple in autumn colours, ivy, needles, grass, green and dried leaves) plus bark materials. These are flat leaf cut-outs for building tree and bush cards, useful for the maple glen and for ground litter. They are not finished trees.
- Skies: 437 HDRIs, tiny at 1K-2K (2.5-10 MB), suitable for sky and reflections.

Not good for:
- Ready-made 3D models. The models section is small and is mostly scanned small objects; there are no weapons, buildings, vehicles, characters or arms, and no finished trees. Only 5 terrain pieces, each too large to commit.
- Anything specifically Japanese (signage, vending machines, street furniture) - not covered.

Memory and repository fit: 1K-JPG packs are about 7-10 MB, 2K-JPG about 24-36 MB, both under the 100 MB limit and appropriate for an 8 GB card. Recommended default: 2K for large ground and facade surfaces seen up close, 1K for everything else.
sources.unverified:
- Count and content of the 3D Model category: the API filter value I tried did not work and the website list page did not return item names to the fetch tool, so "small, mostly scanned props, no weapons/buildings" is from prior knowledge, not confirmed today.
- Exact map list and file names inside a zip (Color, NormalGL, NormalDX, Roughness, Displacement, AmbientOcclusion, Opacity for atlases) and whether model downloads come as OBJ/glTF/USD: the asset page only said the maps are "USDZ-compatible"; no zip was downloaded, per instructions.

- Only 14 of the 30 leaf atlases were visible in the fetched response; the rest were truncated.
- The logo-use rules come from a paraphrased summary of https://docs.ambientcg.com/brand/, not exact quotes.
- No dedicated FAQ page was found on the docs site; the homepage contains a short FAQ that restates CC0. No statement on AI training exists on any page read.
- I did not individually inspect atlas/decal assets for visible trademarks or third-party artwork; the graffiti caution is a general CC0 point, not a finding about a specific asset.

sources.source: Sketchfab (sketchfab.com) - free downloadable 3D models uploaded by users. Ownership changed: sold by Epic Games to KitBash in August 2026 (site footer now reads "KitBash SF Operations LLC"). Store is closed; free downloads still running.
sources.licence_summary:
There is no single Sketchfab licence: every model carries its own, chosen by the uploader. Nothing in any of them restricts the game engine, so Godot is fine.

Usable in a sold game:
- CC0 Public Domain: yes, no credit needed.
- CC Attribution (CC BY 4.0): yes, with credit. This is the bulk of the free library.
- Free Standard (Sketchfab's own licence on some free downloads): commercial use allowed, no credit needed, but the model must not be extractable as a stand-alone file. The full legal text I could open only describes a paid licence, so treat Free Standard as second choice.

Avoid:
- CC BY-SA: commercial use allowed, but modified versions must carry the same licence. How far that reaches into a game is a legal grey area.
- CC BY-ND: commercial use allowed, but modified versions cannot be distributed. Converting, decimating or re-texturing for Godot is modification, so impractical.
- CC BY-NC, BY-NC-SA, BY-NC-ND: no commercial use. Never.
- Editorial: no commercial use. Never.
- Standard (paid): no longer purchasable on Sketchfab; those models now sell on Fab.

Credit for CC BY: Sketchfab's template is "This work is based on [model name] by [author] licensed under CC BY 4.0", with links. Its help page only says to put it alongside the published work; a credits screen plus a credits text file shipped with the game is the normal way to meet it (my reading, not Sketchfab's wording). The licence in force is the one at download time, even if the author changes it later, so record model URL, author, licence and date for every download.

sources.how_to_filter:
On sketchfab.com/search: choose Models, turn on "Downloadable", then open the licence filter and tick only "CC0 Public Domain" and "CC Attribution" (optionally "Free Standard"). Leave ShareAlike, NoDerivs, NonCommercial and Editorial unticked.

Licence IDs, confirmed from Sketchfab's own API list (https://api.sketchfab.com/v3/licenses): CC BY = 322a749bcfa841b29dff1e8a1bb74b0b, CC0 = 7c23a1ba438d4306920229c12afcb5f9, Free Standard = 72eb2b1960364637901eacce19283624.

The website search URL pattern I believe works is https://sketchfab.com/search?features=downloadable&licenses=322a749bcfa841b29dff1e8a1bb74b0b&licenses=7c23a1ba438d4306920229c12afcb5f9&type=models&q=<generic term> - but the page returned empty to my fetcher, so the parameter names are unverified; the UI route above is the safe one.

Always re-read the licence line on the individual model page before downloading: the filter is a convenience, the model page is the record. Prefer the glTF/GLB download option for Godot and check the texture resolution and triangle count shown under "Model information".
sources.account_needed: Downloading needs a free Sketchfab account (login) - this is from prior knowledge, not confirmed on a page I could open today. Browsing and filtering need no account. I did not sign in, download, or accept anything.
sources.quality_for_this_game: Mixed, and it needs hand-picking. The strongest fit is realistic props and clutter for a Japanese city (vending machines, signage, utility poles, street furniture, shrine and park items), photoscanned rocks, trunks and ground debris, and weapon attachments or reference meshes. Many uploads are raw photoscans with millions of triangles, 4K-8K textures and no LODs, so most picks will need decimating and texture downsizing to 1K-2K before they fit an 8 GB budget; single files can also exceed the 100 MB repository limit. Stylised and low-poly content is common, so filter visually. For vegetation it is weaker than dedicated libraries: few foliage sets come with LODs or wind-ready setup. For weapon materials it gives whole textured models, not reusable material sets. I did not survey specific models in this pass, so no individual asset is recommended here.
sources.risks:
1. Per-item licences: the licence is set per model by the uploader. One wrong tick (NC, ND, SA, Editorial) makes a model unusable. Check each model page and keep a log (URL, author, licence, date, screenshot).

2. Uploader may not own the rights: Sketchfab does not vet uploads. Models ripped from other games, or rebuilt from paid packs, are sometimes posted with a CC tag; a CC licence from someone who does not own the work gives no protection. Avoid anything that looks like it came from a known game, has a new or empty uploader profile, or says "ripped", "extracted" or "port" in the description. Community reports of stolen assets staying up until individually reported exist (anecdotal forum posts, not verified).

3. Brands and trademarks: a CC licence covers the 3D model's copyright only, not the logos or product designs on it. Real gun maker names and markings, car makes, drink and convenience-store brands, railway company liveries and real signage are a separate trademark risk in a sold game. Prefer unbranded models or remove the markings. I could not find any Sketchfab wording addressing this.

4. Scans of real places, artworks and people: museum and heritage scans are often NC or carry extra conditions; scans of recognisable people, modern sculptures or buildings can raise rights beyond the licence. Skip them for a commercial game.

5. Attribution load: every CC BY model needs author, title, licence and link in the credits. Twenty models means twenty credit lines; missing one is a breach.

6. ShareAlike and NoDerivs: both technically permit commercial use but create real problems (licence inheritance; no modified versions). Treat as not usable.

7. Free Standard: the published full licence text describes a paid licence and forbids making the asset extractable as a stand-alone file. A shipped Godot game packs assets, which is the normal reading of compliance, but committing the raw file to a public repository would breach it. The same applies to CC BY in reverse: public repo is fine with credit.

8. AI clauses: the NoAI tag is about feeding models into generative-AI training, not about an AI assistant importing the file into a game. It has no effect on game use. The Standard licence text I read has no AI clause.

9. Change of ownership and terms: Sketchfab moved from Epic to KitBash in August 2026. The licence page still calls Sketchfab a division of Epic while the footer names KitBash, so the legal pages are in transition and terms may be rewritten. Epic said in 2024 that free downloads would eventually end on Sketchfab with notice; no date was ever given and the new owner's plan is not stated. Download and log what is needed sooner rather than later; a licence already granted at download time stays valid.

10. Fab overlap: only CC BY and Standard models could migrate to Fab. The same model may exist on both sites under different terms; use the licence from the site actually downloaded from.

sources.risks:
1. UE-only trap: Epic-published sample packs (City Sample Buildings, City Sample Vehicles, City Sample Crowds, and likely the other Epic samples) say "UE-Only" in the description while the Details box says "Standard License". A forum bug report about this contradiction has no Epic answer. Do not use these in Godot. Always read the description text, not only the Details box.
2. Legacy licence: listings migrated from the old Unreal Marketplace may still show "UE Marketplace License" under License terms; that one is Unreal-only. Only accept "Standard License" or CC BY.
3. Format trap: many free Fab listings (and all Megaplants) contain Unreal-format files only. Legally fine for Godot under Standard, but no glTF/FBX is provided. Filter by format.
4. Old Bridge downloads: Megascans files obtained years ago through Quixel Bridge under the old Unreal-only terms are not covered; get them again from Fab under the Standard Licence (this point comes from forum posts, not the EULA itself).
5. Extraction clause: the game must restrict players from extracting the assets. Godot PCK files are easy to unpack, so add a line to the game's own EULA forbidding extraction and consider PCK encryption. Do not ship a level editor or mod tool that exports these assets.
6. Repository: assets may only be shared with collaborators in a private repository. The game's Git repository must stay private if Fab files are committed to it.
7. Licence mixing: do not combine Standard Licence assets with GPL or CC BY-SA content/add-ons.
8. CC BY listings on Fab need visible credit; per-item licences vary, so record licence, URL and date for every download.
9. AI flags are per listing: Megascans now shows "Allows usage with AI: Yes"; many other listings are tagged NoAI and may not be fed to generative AI tools (ordinary AI-assisted integration in the engine is not training, but do not use NoAI items as image-generation inputs). Listings also flag "Generated with AI".
10. Change-of-terms history: Megascans was free for all in late 2024, became paid in 2025, and is free again from Nov 2026. Epic's post does not say "permanent". Add wanted items to the library now; acquired items keep the terms in force at acquisition (EULA s.7(a)). Epic does not guarantee re-download, so keep backups.
11. Revenue tier: Personal tier requires under USD 100,000 gross revenue (including funding raised) in the prior 12 months at acquisition time.
12. Memory/size: Megascans scans are high texel density (the checked item is about 5,900 px/m with nine maps). Pick the lowest quality tier offered and downscale to 1K-2K; raw tiers will blow the 8 GB budget and the 100 MB per-file limit.
13. No warranty: marketplace sellers other than Epic give no guarantee their content is clean of third-party rights or real brand logos; weapon and vehicle models from third-party sellers can carry trademarks.

sources.source: Meshy (meshy.ai) and Tripo (tripo3d.ai) - AI text/image-to-3D generators, free tiers
sources.licence_summary:
The two free tiers differ sharply.

MESHY free plan: usable in a commercially sold Godot game, but only WITH credit. Meshy's terms (last updated 19 Sept 2026) say Meshy owns free-plan output and licenses it to the free user under CC BY 4.0, provided the user credits Meshy. The pricing page labels it "commercial use with attribution". Meshy's suggested credit line is "Model created with Meshy - CC BY 4.0 License" (put it in the game's credits screen and store page/readme). Free allowance: 100 credits per month, up to 10 assets, 10 downloads limited to the "Meshy 6 Lite" model, 1 concurrent task, low queue priority. No engine restriction; Godot is fine. Paid plans (from about GBP 16/month Pro, 1,000 credits) give private, customer-owned assets with no credit required.

TRIPO free plan: NOT usable in a sold game. Tripo's pricing page states the free plan is "Public Models - Non-Commercial Use", and its terms (last updated 11 July 2025), section 5.2.1, say Tripo retains all rights in free users' inputs and outputs. Tripo's own help page says commercial use is "Not granted" to free users. Free allowance: 200 credits per month (about 13 models), 1 concurrent task, 15 exports (H2.5 model only), storage for 10 models, 1 day of edit history. Commercial use needs a paid plan (Pro USD 20/month, 3,000 credits, "Private Models - Commercial Use"); Tripo's help page explicitly lists use in a commercial game on Steam as allowed for paid users. The terms contain no CC BY or attribution clause at all, so the widely repeated claim that Tripo free output is CC BY 4.0 is not supported by Tripo's current terms.

Bottom line: Meshy free = allowed in the paid game with a Meshy credit; Tripo free = not allowed, treat as preview only unless a month of Pro is bought and the assets are generated during that paid period.

sources.risks:
1. Tripo free tier is a licence trap: non-commercial, Tripo keeps all rights, models are public. Many blogs (and some of Tripo's own marketing blog posts) still say "CC BY 4.0, commercial with credit"; the current terms and pricing page say otherwise. Do not ship any Tripo free-tier model.
2. Tripo's help pages contradict each other (one says copyright "belongs entirely to you" but is written for paid users). The terms page is the authoritative one. Whether upgrading later converts earlier free-tier models to commercial is not stated; assume it does not and regenerate while on a paid plan.
3. Meshy free tier: attribution is mandatory (CC BY 4.0), Meshy remains the owner, and the generations are not private. Anyone else may reuse the same model. Keep a log per asset: date, plan, prompt/input image, credit line.
4. Meshy Community page models are a separate trap: the terms mention CC BY-NonCommercial 4.0 for community content (and CC0 for some customer output) and free users cannot download community models anyway. Only use models generated in the owner's own account.
5. AI training: Meshy trains on non-Enterprise content unless opted out by emailing support; Tripo may use free-user content. Neither affects shipping rights, but do not upload anything confidential.
6. Input-image risk on both: the licence covers the 3D output, not the picture fed in. Generating from a photo of a real branded gun, a copyrighted concept image or a trademarked product can still infringe. Use own photos or own-generated concept art; keep real gun maker names/logos off the models.
7. Copyright in purely AI-generated output is legally weak in several countries, so these assets may not be protectable as the owner's exclusive property; and both sets of terms can change (Meshy's were updated Sept 2026), so save a dated copy of the terms on the day of generation.
8. Storefront disclosure: Steam asks developers to declare AI-generated content in the content survey.
9. Quality and technical risk for a realism-first game: raw output is typically very dense (hundreds of thousands to over a million triangles), triangulated with poor edge flow, sometimes non-manifold with flipped normals, auto-unwrapped UVs with many tiny islands, a single material slot, lighting/shadows baked into the colour texture, weak or invented roughness/metal maps, soft melted small details and unreadable text, arbitrary scale and origin, no LODs or collision. Hard-surface items (guns, vehicles, buildings) and first-person-view items look wrong up close. Foliage with thin leaves generates badly.
10. Free-tier quality caps: Meshy free downloads are limited to the Lite model; Tripo free exports are limited to the H2.5 model. The best models and retopology tools are paid.
sources.how_to_filter:
There is nothing to filter on a library page; what matters is the plan the model was generated under.
- Meshy: generate inside the owner's own account only (do not take models from the Community page). Free plan output = CC BY 4.0, add the credit "Model created with Meshy - CC BY 4.0 License". Export as GLB (or FBX) for Godot.
- Tripo: free-plan models are not usable in the sold game. Only models generated while on Pro or higher qualify.
Blender cleanup needed before Godot (same for both tools):
1. Import GLB, set real-world scale in metres, put the origin at the base, apply transforms.
2. Merge by distance, recalculate normals outward, delete loose/internal geometry, fix non-manifold parts.
3. Reduce triangles: Decimate for static props (aim roughly 2k-15k triangles), or remesh/retopologise for anything seen close up; then bake the detail of the dense mesh into a normal map on the light mesh.
4. Re-unwrap UVs if the automatic ones are fragmented; rebake the colour texture.
5. Remove baked lighting from the colour map as far as possible, author proper roughness/metal maps, resize textures to 1K-2K.
6. Split material slots where needed, make 2-3 LODs (or let Godot generate them on import), add a simple collision shape.
7. Export GLB, keep each file well under 100 MB.
sources.quality_for_this_game: Low to moderate fit. Reasonable use: small background clutter seen from a few metres (rubbish bags, crates, vending-machine-style props, rocks, stumps, shrine/park ornaments, debris) after Blender cleanup, and as rough blockouts. Poor fit: weapons and first-person arms (seen at centimetres, need exact hard-surface edges - the existing dimension-accurate gun models with scanned PBR materials from a CC0 texture library will look far better), buildings (the generated mid-rises plus real scanned facade textures beat AI meshes), and vegetation (thin leaves and branches come out as blobs; scanned plant libraries are the right source). Given the owner rejects anything that looks low quality, expect most raw generations to be rejected; only cleaned-up mid-distance props are likely to pass. The free allowances are small anyway: about 10 models a month on Meshy, and Tripo's roughly 13 a month cannot be shipped.

No account was created and no terms were accepted during this research. Meshy free: 100 credits/month, 10 downloads. Tripo free: 200 credits/month, 15 exports, non-commercial.

sources.licence_summary:
All statements below are for a paid, closed-source game made in Godot. None of the sources read imposes any engine restriction.

SAFE, NO CREDIT NEEDED (read on the source's own page today):
- 3dtextures.me: CC0, commercial use allowed, no credit. Realistic PBR textures.
- cgbookcase: CC0 1.0, no credit; 582 PBR textures, 1K-8K. Realistic.
- TextureCan: CC0 1.0, commercial use allowed, no credit, may ship with your project. Realistic.
- ShareTextures: commercial use allowed, no credit, but it is a "custom CC0" with added limits (no redistribution as collections; no use in hateful/violent/illegal content). Realistic textures and some models.
- Kenney: CC0, commercial allowed, no credit. STYLISED low-poly - not suitable for this game's visuals (only useful for UI icons/prototype placeholders).
- Quaternius: CC0, commercial allowed, no credit. STYLISED low-poly - not suitable.
- Blendkit (BlenderKit was renamed in June 2026): two licences only, Royalty Free and CC0; both allow commercial use without credit and use inside a game. Royalty Free forbids reselling the model as a model/asset pack. Mixed quality, many realistic items. Now has a Godot plugin (early-stage).

SAFE WITH CONDITIONS:
- Textures.com free account: its FAQ (read via search result, page itself is script-rendered and would not open) allows commercial games including with free-account downloads, but forbids open-source release of the images. Realistic. Free tier is credit-limited and low resolution.
- Mixamo (Adobe): characters and animations royalty-free for commercial games, no credit; raw files may not be redistributed. Official FAQ page returned 403, so this rests on search results of Adobe pages - treat as likely but not directly read.
- CGTrader free models: licence chosen per item by the seller. Default Royalty Free allows use embedded in a game, with a duty to stop players extracting the file. Items marked Editorial may NOT be used in a game.
- Smithsonian Open Access 3D: items marked CC0 are free for commercial use with no credit; unmarked items need written permission (official FAQ returned 403; from search result of that FAQ). Realistic scans, mostly museum objects - limited relevance.
- NASA 3D: generally not copyrighted in the US, commercial use allowed if no endorsement is implied and NASA logos are not used. Limited relevance (aircraft/space props).

PER-ITEM LICENCE, CHECK EVERY ASSET:
- Godot Asset Library: every asset carries its own licence (MIT, CC0, CC-BY, GPL, CC-BY-SA, Proprietary). MIT/CC0/BSD/zlib/Apache are fine; avoid GPL/AGPL and CC-BY-SA.
- OpenGameArt: mix of CC0, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, GPL, OGA-BY. Use CC0 only (or OGA-BY with credit). Mostly stylised/2D; little that is realistic enough.
- itch.io free asset packs: no site-wide licence; each creator sets terms. Mostly stylised.
- Free3D: licence per model, many free models are labelled personal-use only. Do not use unless the item page states commercial use.
- Thingiverse/Printables: per-model Creative Commons, many non-commercial; print meshes are not game-ready. Not recommended.

NOT FREE FOR THIS GAME:

sources.risks:
- Per-item licences: Godot Asset Library, OpenGameArt, itch.io, CGTrader, Free3D, Thingiverse/Printables and Blendkit all need the licence checked and recorded per asset. Avoid GPL/AGPL, CC-BY-SA, any NC (non-commercial), ND (no derivatives), "personal use" and CGTrader "Editorial" items.
- Repository exposure: the game repo commits binaries. If the repo is ever public, raw files from Textures.com, Blendkit Royalty Free, CGTrader Royalty Free and Mixamo would count as forbidden redistribution; ShareTextures also bars redistribution as collections. Only true CC0 sources (3dtextures.me, cgbookcase, TextureCan, Kenney, Quaternius, CC0 Blendkit items) are safe in a public repo. Keep the repo private or keep these files out of it.
- CGTrader requires reasonable measures to stop players extracting the model; Godot's .pck is easy to unpack, so use PCK encryption or avoid CGTrader items.
- Textures.com forbids releasing its images under open-source licences, even modified.
- ShareTextures is not plain CC0: it bans use in "hateful, violent, or illegal content". A shooter is probably not what is meant, but the wording is vague; prefer 3dtextures.me/cgbookcase/TextureCan (and Poly Haven/ambientCG) where an equivalent exists.
- OpenGameArt CC-BY/CC-BY-SA 3.0 items carry an anti-DRM clause that may conflict with Steam DRM; use CC0 items only.
- Trademarks: CC0 or royalty-free covers copyright only. Real gun maker names/logos (Glock, FN, CZ, Colt), vehicle badges, Japanese shop/brand signage and NASA insignia inside a model or texture are not cleared. Strip or replace markings.
- Smithsonian: only items showing the CC0 mark; third-party and cultural-sensitivity limits still apply.
- AI clauses: CGTrader bars free downloads from machine-learning use; Mixamo reportedly excludes ML training. Using the assets in the game via an AI coding assistant is not training, but do not feed them to model-training or image-to-3D services that claim training rights.
- Terms change: Blendkit was renamed and restructured in 2026 (paid tiers changed); Mixamo is reported by a third party to be in maintenance mode. Save a dated copy/screenshot of the licence page and the item page for every asset shipped.
- Memory: cgbookcase and ShareTextures default to 4K-8K; download 1K-2K or downscale.
sources.quality_for_this_game:
Realistic and useful:
- 3dtextures.me, cgbookcase, TextureCan, ShareTextures: realistic tileable PBR sets (concrete, asphalt, plaster, tiles, metal, wood, bark, ground, moss). Good for park buildings, pavements, walls and for gun materials (parkerised/blued steel, anodised aluminium, polymer, rubber grips). PNG/JPG maps import straight into Godot. Pick 1K-2K.
- Blendkit free plan: largest pool of realistic free models and materials here (trees, plants, street furniture, architecture props). Quality varies item by item; materials are Blender node setups that need baking to PBR maps before export to GLB. Many models are render-grade with high triangle counts and no LODs.
- Mixamo: realistic motion-capture animation (walk, run, crouch, death, idle) for third-person bodies and AI/robots-as-humanoids; FBX imports to Godot with retargeting. Not a fix for the first-person arms model (no FPS arm rigs or weapon animations).
- Textures.com free: realistic photos/decals (signage, grime, leaks) but free tier is small daily credits and low resolution; marginal.
- CGTrader free section: some realistic weapons, vehicles and Japanese props, but licence, trademarks and poly count must be vetted per item.
- Smithsonian / NASA: realistic scans, but subject matter (museum objects, spacecraft) rarely fits; possible airport set-dressing later.

Stylised - reject for visuals: Kenney, Quaternius, most of OpenGameArt, most itch.io free packs. Godot Asset Library is mainly code/tools/shaders (useful for sky, water, foliage wind, decals - check licence is MIT/CC0), not hero art. Thingiverse/Printables/Free3D: not game-ready and licence-risky; skip.
sources.how_to_filter:
- 3dtextures.me, cgbookcase, TextureCan, Kenney, Quaternius: whole site is one licence; no filter needed. On cgbookcase use the minimum-resolution filter and download the 1K/2K variant.
- ShareTextures: download only from sharetextures.com itself (licence applies only to direct downloads).
- Blendkit: in the search filters tick Free, and where possible restrict licence to CC0; note each asset's licence (Royalty Free or CC0) shown on its page.
- Godot Asset Library (godotengine.org/asset-library/asset): use the licence filter/sort; accept MIT, CC0, BSD, zlib, Apache, Unlicense, CC-BY (with credit); reject GPL/LGPL/AGPL, CC-BY-SA, Proprietary.
- OpenGameArt: in the search form's licence field select CC0 only (optionally OGA-BY).
- itch.io: browse Game assets > Free, then read each pack's page for a stated licence (look for CC0 or explicit commercial-use permission); no reliable site licence filter was verified.
- CGTrader: Free filter, then on each item check the licence line says Royalty Free (not Editorial, not a custom licence).
- Free3D: use only items whose page explicitly shows a commercial-use licence; skip "Personal Use".
- Smithsonian (3d.si.edu): use only items showing the CC0 icon.
- Exact URL parameters for these filters were not verified.
sources.account_needed: No account: Kenney, Quaternius, 3dtextures.me, cgbookcase, TextureCan, ShareTextures, NASA 3D, Smithsonian, Godot Asset Library (also built into the Godot editor), OpenGameArt downloads. Account required: Textures.com (free account, one per person), Blendkit (free account plus add-on/plugin), Mixamo (free Adobe ID, no subscription), CGTrader and Free3D (free account to download). itch.io: usually no account for free packs. Account creation must be done by the owner personally; I did not sign in or accept terms anywhere.

- Textures.com: terms and FAQ pages are script-rendered and returned only a tagline; quotes come from search-result excerpts of textures.com/faq-license. Current free-tier credit and resolution limits not confirmed.
- OpenGameArt: FAQ returned 403; licence list and the CC-BY DRM issue come from search results of OGA forum threads, not the live FAQ.
- Smithsonian: both FAQ URLs returned 403; CC0/commercial statement from search-result excerpt of the official FAQ.
- Free3D: licence page returned 403; "personal use only" labelling is from third-party sources.
- Thingiverse/Printables: no official licence page opened (Prusa help URL 404); information from third-party guides.
- itch.io: only the creator FAQ was read; it is silent on asset licences, so "per creator" is an inference.
- Godot Asset Library: no statement of permitted licences found; list taken from the filter options.
- cgbookcase: dedicated licence page not found (404); CC0 statement read on the textures listing page.
- Blendkit: free-plan size and paid prices come from news reports with conflicting figures; Godot plugin quality untested.

needs.dead_ends: Honest gaps and exclusions. (1) No free, game-ready, LOD-equipped whole SAKURA tree, BAMBOO grove or Japanese black pine exists under CC0/CC BY that I could find; these must be assembled from scans/atlases (ffish.asia + Poly Haven bark) or come from Megascans if the Fab listings check out. (2) Reeds, cattails, susuki/miscanthus: Sketchfab searches returned nothing usable; no CC0 rice-paddy field kit either (only single scanned rice plants). (3) Megascans: free status confirmed only through two news articles dated 6 Nov 2026; the Fab pages would not render listings for me, so the per-item licence and whether plants are 'Standard' or 'UE-Only' is unverified. (4) Sketchfab item pages returned empty to the fetch tool; licences were read from Sketchfab's own API record for each model (api.sketchfab.com/v3/models/<id>), which carries the same licence field. (5) Excluded: xfrog plants on Sketchfab (Nikko maple, jasmine, forsythia) are CC BY-NC-ND; 'Japanese Maple' by dipietron and 'Hedge' by 1-3D.com are CC BY-SA (share-alike, avoid); ShareTextures.com calls itself 'Custom CC0' but its licence page bans use in 'violent' content and automated downloads, which is risky for a shooter, so not recommended. (6) Poly Haven has no bamboo, cherry or maple models, and its full trees are 2M-17M triangles. (7) ambientCG's 3D model list could not be read (page too long), so its 3D stumps/logs are unchecked. (8) Visual quality was judged from descriptions and metadata only; nothing was downloaded or viewed, so each Sketchfab item needs a look in the viewer before use. (9) Tripo/Meshy were not researched for this need: AI-generated foliage is generally poor (alpha-card leaves do not survive generation).

finds.what_it_is: Game-ready realistic tree packs built for real-time use: each tree has LOD0-LOD3 plus a billboard, shared bark and branch atlases, and vertex colours prepared for wind (R = baked AO, G = wind gradient).

finds.work_needed: Add a credit line for LOLIPOP in the game credits. Split the pack into one scene per tree, wire LODs into Godot visibility ranges, set leaf material to alpha-scissor with backlight, hook the green vertex channel into the wind shader. Maples are European-style acer, not Japanese palmatum: recolour the leaf atlas and reduce scale for a Japanese look. Downsize the oak 4K atlases to 2K. Look at the model in the viewer first to confirm it meets the owner's realism bar; I judged from descriptions, not from renders.

finds.why_it_fits: Lets the AI produce any number of unique trunk-and-branch skeletons at a chosen budget, then dress them with CC0 Poly Haven bark and ambientCG or ffish.asia leaf atlases, giving Japanese species with full control over LODs.
finds.work_needed: Replace the bundled textures with the CC0 ones above so the texture question disappears. Generate 3 detail levels per tree for LODs. Looks only as real as the leaf atlas applied.

check.licence_seen: MIT License. The repository page (https://github.com/dgreenheck/ez-tree) shows the label "MIT license". The LICENSE file (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dgreenheck/ez-tree/main/LICENSE) reads "MIT License", "Copyright (c) 2024 Daniel Greenheck", and "Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy". The grant includes the right to sell.
check.note:
The MIT licence is confirmed and permits commercial use, but the bundled bark and leaf textures are a provenance risk.

- **Availability:** the repository is live and shows no archived notice (134 commits, open issues and pull requests). The Releases section is empty; the tool is used through the eztree.dev web app or as a library. The README says the app can "export as .PNG or .GLB files". I did not open eztree.dev or test an export.
- **Texture risk:** neither the README nor the LICENSE mentions the bark and leaf textures, their source or any credits. The LICENSE covers only "Software" and "associated documentation files". The textures sit in the repository with no separate licence, so MIT nominally covers them, but their origin is not stated. Safest use is to take the generated mesh and swap in CC0 bark and leaf textures (for example from Poly Haven or ambientCG).
- **Credit:** MIT requires keeping the copyright and permission notice with copies of the software. Add "EZ-Tree, (c) 2024 Daniel Greenheck, MIT" to the game's credits or licence file.
- **Engine and sale restrictions:** none on the page. It is written with Three.js, but GLB export works in any engine. Nothing forbids use in a sold game.
- **Brands:** no real-world brand names or logos in the asset; the only logos on the page are GitHub and badge chrome.
- **Quality:** these are stylised-to-mid-realism procedural trees, not scan-quality hero assets, and may need material work.

needs.dead_ends:
Checked on the live web on 2026-11-12; nothing was downloaded and no site was signed into.

Not found free and usable:
- Modular Japanese apartment / shop-house KIT (wall, window, balcony, shopfront modules) under CC0 or CC BY: none. Sketchfab results were stylised/anime/low-poly, untextured (Chuo Store, 433k faces, no textures), European (Mega Moduler Apartment Building, 441k faces, Parisian style), NC/ND-licensed photogrammetry, or 'Free Standard' rather than CC (Asian Buildings Set, 299k faces; three 'Japanese Building | CC0' models by LitFor20 whose title says CC0 but whose licence field says Free Standard, so treated as unclear). Poly Haven has no buildings. Kenney and Quaternius city kits are CC0 but stylised, so excluded for realism.
- 'Asian Shop 1/2/4' by abhayexe (about 4.3k faces each, CC Attribution, realistic PBR shop-houses): excluded as unclear origin because the description says the reference images came from an AI chat tool and is stuffed with unrelated keywords.
- Modern tram / light rail under CC0 or CC BY: none realistic and game-weight. CC BY trams found were Soviet/Tatra, sci-fi, or 180k-890k faces; the one Japanese tram result was NC-ND photogrammetry. Only the Free Standard Flexity listed above fits.
- Clean, modern, unbranded parked cars: none. Realistic free cars on Sketchfab are almost all real makes and models (Suzuki, Daihatsu, Toyota), which carry trademark/trade-dress risk regardless of the CC licence; generic ones are low-poly/stylised. Only the wrecked generic sedan and Poly Haven's Covered Car are safe.
- Japanese city bicycle (mamachari): no results. 'Electric Bike' by Bee.Lucas (14k faces) is labelled CC Attribution but its own description says non-commercial and it copies a real Madrid bike-share brand: excluded. 'Bicycle Collection Free' (200k faces, CC BY) was not opened.
- Japanese pedestrian guard fences (white pipe rails), tactile yellow paving, Japanese-design manhole covers: 'Japanese Manhole Covers - Kawaguchiko' (CC BY) is 189k faces with zero textures and hand-painted tags, not usable; ambientCG covers are European patterns.
- Roller-shutter tiling material: ambientCG search for 'shutter' returned 0; use Poly Haven's Rollershutter Door/Window models instead.
- Fab: no free Japanese street listing could be confirmed. The Japanese Utility Pole Set on Fab (https://www.fab.com/listings/212ee993-a021-49b6-a240-15509dcb535c) is paid (GBP 9.78, FBX, 1-70k tris, 2K-4K textures). Fab's licence summary page (https://www.fab.com/eula) says assets may be used with \"any compatible tools (usage is not limited to Unreal Engine)\" and in commercially distributed projects, but the UE-only restriction on Epic-published content was not stated on that page and remains unverified; Fab's free catalogue could not be browsed without a session.
- PLATEAU licence could not be verified at source (mlit.go.jp unreachable).

Caveats that apply to every Sketchfab find: licences were read from Sketchfab's own item data (licence field quoted), but file sizes and included formats are only visible after sign-in and were not checked; visual quality was judged from descriptions, tags and counts, not by viewing the models, so each needs an eyes-on check in the Sketchfab viewer before download. A CC licence from an uploader does not clear third-party logos or brand designs on the model. Meshy and Tripo were not researched in this step.

Licence and availability check out, but the sign textures are a real risk.

- **Availability:** the page is live, titled "Download Free 3D model", with a "Download 3D Model" button; the API reports isDownloadable true and price null. It shows 1,430 downloads, 10.7k triangles, 5.4k vertices, published 18 Oct 2021. Downloading needs a Sketchfab login; I did not sign in or download.

needs.dead_ends:
Not found free and usable, stated plainly:

1. CC0 modern firearms: none. Sketchfab's CC0 + downloadable filter for 'rifle' and 'pistol' returns only museum scans of antique flintlock/percussion guns (200K-300K faces, e.g. Malopolska Virtual Museums, ArmsMuseum) and ~300-face untextured blockouts. The only realistic CC0 guns are Poly Haven's two vintage pieces. 'tactical' with the CC0 filter returned zero results.

2. Free realistic versions of the seven specific guns (Glock 17, M4A1, SVD, M40A5, AW, EVO 3, SCAR 17, Uzi) under CC0: none. CC BY real-gun models exist on Sketchfab (e.g. 'SLR AR-15' by AlexFinsher 41K faces, 'M4A4 carbine pbr' by javadbayat 76K faces, 'Classic M4' by jeandiz 28K faces, 'Low-Poly FN SCAR-H' by notcplkerry 13K faces) but all carry real-brand likeness and I did not open their individual records, so they are leads only, not recommendations. jeandiz's own descriptions say several of his pieces are assembled from community-shared parts, so provenance is uncertain. Since the game's guns are already built to real dimensions, re-texturing them with the CC0 material sets above is lower risk than swapping in these models.

3. Purpose-made gun-finish scans (true blued steel, parkerised steel, cerakote, hard-coat anodise, stippled polymer): no free CC0 set found on ambientCG or Poly Haven. Poly Haven's metal category is almost entirely rust, corrugated iron and shutters - no firearm-suitable metals. The finishes must be built by tinting the generic ambientCG metals/plastics listed.

4. Tactical fabrics (Cordura/ballistic nylon, webbing, ripstop, camouflage): ambientCG API returned 0 results for 'nylon', 'canvas' and 'camouflage'; Poly Haven fabric category has denim, linen, hessian, fleece and leather but no nylon, webbing or camo. A web search surfaced only paid (Poliigon) or unclear-licence sites. ShareTextures, cgbookcase and 3dtextures.me were not checked item-by-item. Closest free stand-ins: Poly Haven 'hessian_230' / 'rough_linen' / 'denim_fabric' weaves recoloured, CC0.

needs.dead_ends:
Honest summary: there is no free, ready-made, realistic first-person arms + full body + complete weapon-handling animation set under CC0. The realistic route is assembly: MPFB body (CC0) + CC BY gloved arms from Sketchfab + Mixamo/Quaternius/100STYLE for body motion + per-gun reloads hand-keyed or adapted from the CC BY Sketchfab sets.
- Sketchfab CC0: searches for fps arms, realistic rigged male, male hands, tactical gloves, and scanned jackets with the CC0 filter all returned zero results. Everything usable there is CC Attribution.
- Excluded for licence: GDQuest 'godot-4-fps-arms' (code MIT, but LICENSE says art assets are CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0); Bandai Namco Research motion datasets (README: CC BY-NC 4.0 for both); LAFAN1/AMASS-style research sets are non-commercial by reputation and were not pursued.
- CMU mocap: the official site (mocap.cs.cmu.edu) did not resolve, so its terms are UNVERIFIED. Secondary sources say it may be included in sold products but not resold; one FBX conversion (4TU) carries a conflicting CC BY-NC 4.0 label. Not recommended until the FAQ can be read; quality is also dated and has no fingers.
- 'Meta' mocap library: no free commercially usable Meta motion library was found; nothing verified.
- Fab: no free first-person arms listing found. The listings that looked free are paid (GAMICO 'FPS Arms Rigged' about 5 GBP, Polly Creative 'Hand Models' about 4 GBP); free FPS animation entries are demos of paid packs. Fab licence summary does allow non-Unreal engines (\"usage is not limited to Unreal Engine\") and forbids standalone redistribution; Epic's own sample content (mannequins, Game Animation Sample, MetaHuman) is Unreal-only and was excluded.
- Unclear licence, not recommended: Kevin Iglesias 'Human Soldier Animations FREE' (128 clips with reloads, Godot build, 16 MB, but the page states no licence terms); CGTrader free 'Game Ready FPS Arms' (page did not load; label reported as 'Royalty Free No Ai License', unverified); Renderpeople free rigged people (commercial use stated mainly for visualisation, games not addressed, 8K textures); Reallusion ActorCore free motions (2022 report says games need a separate distribution licence); MoCap Online free packs (page returned HTTP 429, unverified).
- Pages that could not be opened directly: Adobe's official Mixamo FAQ (HTTP 403), blender.org demo-files page (HTTP 403), Sketchfab HTML item pages (empty; licences were read from Sketchfab's own model records instead), itch 'Animated FPS Pistol' (404).
- Not found at all: free realistic bare male hands with skin textures at game resolution; free first-person reload sets specific to M4A1, SCAR 17, SVD, bolt-action rifles (M40A5, AW), Scorpion EVO or Uzi; free first-person crouch/lean/vault handling animations; free civilian near-future Japanese clothing sets.
- Repository caution: Mixamo and Rokoko files must not be redistributed raw, so they should not be committed to a public repository; only the CC0 and CC BY items are safe to commit (CC BY items need a credits file).

- Blender developer docs pages for the bundle (https://developer.blender.org/docs/release_notes/4.0/asset_bundles/ and https://developer.blender.org/docs/features/asset_system/asset_bundles/human_base_meshes/) opened fine but carry no licence statement for the bundle; they only point to the Demo Files page for download. Their footer CC-BY-SA 4.0 notice covers the documentation text, not the bundle.
- No engine restriction or ban on use in a sold game was seen in any source that opened. No brand names or logos were mentioned; the contents are generic anatomy base meshes (realistic and stylized bodies, heads, hands, feet, eye, jaw).
- Quality/fit: these are untextured, unrigged sculpting base meshes meant for the Multiresolution modifier, shipped as a .blend asset library. They are a starting point for characters, not game-ready assets, and would need retopology/UVs/rigging/textures. They are not vegetation, building or weapon assets.

needs.dead_ends:
How licences were read: Poly Haven, ambientCG, Sonniss, Pixabay and Freesound pages were opened directly. Sketchfab item pages are script-rendered and came back empty, so each Sketchfab licence above was read from Sketchfab's own public record for that exact item (api.sketchfab.com/v3/models/<id>), which returns the licence label and the 'Commercial use is allowed' requirement; texture resolutions and file sizes were often not readable there. Fab listing pages opened, but the 'License terms' field rendered as '-', so no Fab licence is verified per listing. Nothing was downloaded, no sign-in, no terms accepted.

Not found free and usable:
- CC0 on Sketchfab for these subjects: none. Every usable container, forklift, pallet, torii, lantern, house, hangar and drone was CC Attribution (credit required); the CC0 filter on Sketchfab's search returned nothing for these terms.
- Airport terminal parts, jet bridge, boarding stairs, tug: nothing realistic and commercially licensed. Fab's free 'airport' results were unrelated or stylised. Two good-looking scanned hangars on Sketchfab are CC BY-NC (excluded).
- Runway markings (numbers, threshold bars, centreline): no dedicated free asset; only ambientCG road-line decals as a stand-in.
- Quayside ship-to-shore container crane: only one untextured 131k-triangle CAD-style model (CC BY) on Sketchfab; the Poly Haven crane is an indoor overhead type. A free 'Tower Crane' exists on Fab (https://www.fab.com/listings/71a0da29-31aa-4496-8ecd-585a2cb57f4b), not opened, licence unverified.
- Mooring bollards: Sketchfab ones are million-triangle heritage scans (CC BY, need heavy decimation) or non-commercial. On Fab, 'Tee Mooring Bollard 30t - Game Ready PBR' (https://www.fab.com/listings/c65ec8c6-5e9a-48b3-8c3c-9210ae0710ce) and 'Shipping Container 20ft ISO - Game Ready PBR' (https://www.fab.com/listings/4eba334e-9304-46bd-a4cd-3a719511d569) by Model Studio are free, FBX, 2K textures, with three LODs (about 19k/8.5k/2.8k triangles) - attractive specs, but the licence line was not shown and the listings disclose they were procedurally generated with AI-written scripts, so treat as unclear until the owner checks the licence when signed in.
- Dam or industrial plant as a set piece: nothing game-ready. Dam models on Sketchfab are 2-3 million-triangle drone scans, map-data rips (Hoover Dam 'imported from Google Maps data' - unclear origin, avoid), or AI-generated. Best route is to build the dam from generated concrete geometry dressed with the Poly Haven pipes, crane and generator.
- Robots: no realistic free security or quadruped robot with clear provenance. The only quadruped hits ('Sci-Fi Robotic Hound', 'Sci-Fi Spider Drone' by zaina, CC BY, about 17.5k triangles, 2K textures, https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/57a62086626947648b9dfa1859afb03a) state they were 'Created using Rapid Assets AI', are unrigged and unanimated, and would need fixing in Blender; listed here as a fallback only. Fab's free robot/drone results were mostly stylised or concept sketches.
- Japanese material on Fab beyond Megascans street props: a Quixel-only 'japanese' search returned nothing; no free realistic shrine building or rural house on Fab.
- Japanese station door chimes and departure melodies: no CC0 recording verified (Freesound returned a rate-limit error on that search). Caution: real Japanese station melodies and announcements are copyrighted compositions/recordings even inside a 'CC0' field recording, so a chime should be newly made rather than taken from a recording.
- Pixabay sound effects: licence summary read (https://pixabay.com/service/license-summary/ - free, no attribution, no standalone redistribution), which permits use inside a game, but no specific Pixabay sound was opened or verified, and uploads there are user-submitted with no provenance check, so prefer Sonniss and Freesound CC0.
- OpenGameArt 'gunshot sounds' (reported CC0 by search) returned HTTP 403, so unverified.
- Megascans 'free again' (5 Nov 2026) is based on CG Channel's report; the primary Epic announcement and the Creative Bloq article could not be read in full.

- GDC 2026 bundle: it is not on the claimed page. It lives at https://gdc.sonniss.com/ (five zips, about 7.47 GB, 347+ files, Google Drive mirrors and torrent) and links to the same licence. The archive page says there was no 2025 bundle.
- Sold games: allowed. FAQ: "you can absolutely sell them as part of your finished game, film, app, or creative project."
- Engine restriction: none on the page or in the licence.
- Restrictions that do apply:
  - No redistributing or reselling the raw sounds, including as a sound library, sample pack or asset pack. Licence: "Licensee may not sell any of the sound effects as they come."
  - Scope is "licensed for media production (games, film, TV, interactive projects) only."
  - AI/ML training on the sounds is prohibited.
  - Do not claim you recorded the originals.
- Practical consequence: ship the sounds only inside the built game, and do not commit the raw files to a public repository, since that would amount to redistributing them as sound effects.
- Brands: audio only, so no logos in the assets. The page names no contributor brands or branded-product recordings; the only logos are a "Trusted By" client strip and payment icons. The licence has no trademark clause. Individual file names inside the bundles (gun or vehicle model names, for example) were not inspected.
- Quality was not assessed, since nothing was downloaded.

result.gaps:
COMPLETENESS CRITIC REPORT (checked live 2026-11-12; nothing downloaded, no sign-in, no terms accepted)

## Verdict
The pass is thorough on the big libraries. The three most valuable gaps still open are (1) Japanese identity of the city (buildings, signage), (2) the hero trees (sakura, pine, bamboo), (3) realistic first-person hands/arms. None has a free ready-made answer. Each has a free route that needs assembly work, and the finds below are sources the pass did not list.

## Gap 1 - Japanese city identity: buildings and signage

**Find 1a: PLATEAU (Japanese government 3D city models, incl. Tokyo 23 wards)**
- URL read: https://www.geospatial.jp/ckan/dataset/plateau-tokyo23ku
- Licence as shown on that page: governed by the "PLATEAU Site Policy" section 3 (copyright); the page states the data is free for anyone, commercial use included.
- Secondary confirmation: OpenStreetMap wiki lists it as "CC BY 4.0 or ODbL or ODC-BY (Multi-licensed)" (https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/MLIT_PLATEAU, last edited 2022). A search snippet of MLIT's own start guide names the Public Data Licence v1.0, CC BY 4.0, ODC BY and ODbL.
- UNVERIFIED at source: the official policy page https://www.mlit.go.jp/plateau/site-policy/ did not resolve again today (DNS failure). The exact credit wording must be read there before use.
- Formats and size: FBX about 2.8 GB, OBJ about 2.1 GB for the whole 23-ward set, also CityGML and 3D Tiles. LOD1 (plain boxes) covers all wards; LOD2 (roof shapes) covers about 32 km2 of selected districts.
- Honest fit: not street-level quality. Textures, where present, are aerial photos. Good only as a distant skyline/backdrop and as real Tokyo block footprints and heights to drive the generated mid-rises. The archive is far over the 100 MB per-file limit, so only a small cut-out district, decimated and re-exported as GLB, could be committed. Credit line required.

**Find 1b: Japanese road signs as vector art (Wikimedia Commons)**
- URL read: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Japan_road_sign_302.svg (one of a full numbered series "Japan road sign NNN.svg").
- Licence tag on the page: "This work is in the public domain in Japan according to Article 13 of the Copyright Act".
- Caveats: the tag speaks for Japan only; each file has its own page and tag, so read it per sign. Search results show some route-sign files warn that the lettering is outlined from a specific font and its licence must be checked if the text is changed.
- Fit: very good. SVG renders to small PNG decals at any size, tiny memory cost, and correct signs are a cheap, strong "this is Japan" signal.

**Still missing after this check (needs custom or paid work)**
- Modular Japanese apartment/shopfront kit: still nothing free and realistic. Realistic options are a paid kit, or building facade modules in code/Blender from CC0 materials already found.
- Shop signage and vending-machine faces: must be made new with invented brand names. A Japanese font is needed; Noto Sans JP is the usual choice (SIL Open Font Licence by reputation), but the Google Fonts licence page returned no content today, so UNVERIFIED. Read the OFL.txt inside the download.
- Pedestrian guard rails, tactile paving, mamachari bicycle, Japanese manhole covers: still custom work (all are simple shapes, suitable for code-built or AI-generated-with-cleanup).

## Gap 2 - Hero trees (sakura, Japanese black pine, bamboo)

**Find 2a: EZ-Tree (procedural tree generator, runs in a browser)**
- URLs read: https://github.com/dgreenheck/ez-tree and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dgreenheck/ez-tree/main/LICENSE
- Licence: "MIT License", "Copyright (c) 2024 Daniel Greenheck".
- Exports GLB and PNG. The README documents built-in LOD generation: default switch distances 100 and 250 units, about 40% and 20% of triangles, and a GLB export of a LOD tree includes every level.
- Caveats: README names deciduous/oak/ash types only; pine, cherry and bamboo presets are not mentioned. The README does not say whether the bundled bark and leaf images fall under the MIT licence or where they came from, so swap in Poly Haven bark and the scanned leaf atlases from the earlier pass rather than shipping its bundled textures. Realism is mid-level: fine for mid-distance and background trees, not a close-up hero sakura.

**Find 2b: Tree3D for Godot (gdTree3D)**
- URL read: https://github.com/JekSun97/gdTree3D ; reported as MIT by https://gamefromscratch.com/tree3d-procedural-tree-add-on-for-godot/ . The repo page itself links a LICENSE.md I did not get to open, so MIT is second-hand.
- States "Godot 4.5+ (Windows, Linux, MacOS)". Leaves supported. "Automatic LOD" is listed under "Soon...", so no LODs yet. Wind status is contradictory on the page.
- Fit: fallback only until LOD ships.

**Plain statement:** a close-up, blossom-quality sakura, a shaped black pine and a bamboo grove still do not exist free and game-ready. Options in order of quality: (a) Megascans/Megaplants on Fab if the owner confirms the per-item licence while signed in; (b) a paid tree pack or SpeedTree-made assets; (c) custom assembly (EZ-Tree trunk and branches + scanned sakura petal/leaf cards + Poly Haven bark). Bamboo is the easiest to custom-build (straight segmented culms plus leaf cards). AI generators (Meshy/Tripo) are not suitable for foliage.

## Gap 3 - Realistic first-person hands and arms

**Find 3a: Blender Studio "Human Base Meshes" bundle**
- Licence: "available free under a Creative Commons CC0 licence" (https://www.cgchannel.com/2023/06/download-blender-studios-free-human-base-meshes/). A search snippet of blender.org's own asset-bundle page lists v1.4.1, CC0, about 49 MB, updated 20 Jan 2025, Blender 4.2 LTS or newer.
- UNVERIFIED at source: https://www.blender.org/download/demo-files/ returned HTTP 403 again. The release-notes page (https://developer.blender.org/docs/release_notes/3.6/asset_bundles/) states no bundle licence. Read the licence line on the download page by hand.
- Contents per CG Channel: 17 meshes, realistic and stylised, full male and female bodies plus separate hands, feet and heads; quad topology, UV maps, multi-resolution sculpt detail on the realistic ones.
- Honest fit: this gives properly sculpted realistic hand and forearm geometry under CC0, which was the missing piece. It is NOT game-ready: no skin textures, no rig, and one .blend file. Work needed in Blender: bake the sculpt detail to a normal map on a low-poly hand, add a skin material (CC0 skin textures were not found by the pass either), rig to the existing first-person skeleton. Covering the hands with gloves and sleeves (CC BY gloves from the earlier pass, or fabric/leather CC0 materials) avoids the skin-texture problem entirely and suits a tactical shooter.

**Find 3b: The Base Mesh**
- URL read: https://thebasemesh.com/ . Licence wording: "100% Free. CC0 License." 1250+ models, "UV Unwrapped", basic UVs on every model.
- Formats and textures not stated on the page; these are untextured base meshes. Useful as clean CC0 starting geometry for props the pass could not find (generic unbranded vehicles, bicycles, street furniture, gear) which are then textured with the CC0 materials already listed. Needs an eyes-on check of what is actually in the catalogue.

**Plain statement:** per-gun reload animations for the M4A1, SCAR 17, SVD, bolt-actions, EVO 3 and Uzi remain custom work or a paid animation pack. No free source was found by me either.

## Smaller gaps, checked briefly
- Tactical fabrics (Cordura, webbing, ripstop) and gun finishes: still no CC0 source. 3dtextures.me is confirmed CC0 ("All textures on this site are licensed as CC0", https://3dtextures.me/about/) with redistribution allowed and no content restrictions stated, but a search found no nylon, webbing, carbon-fibre or grip-rubber sets there, only general fabrics (padded, lace, knit). aitextured.com has ripstop and nylon camo sets but under its own "Free Commercial License (FCL) v1.1", not CC0, and the name suggests AI-generated images; licence not read in full, so not recommended. Conclusion: make these procedurally (a weave normal map is a simple generated pattern) or buy one small material pack.
- Unbranded magnified scope, sling, magazines, modern tram, clean cars, airport and port set pieces, robots: unchanged from the pass. These are the best candidates for Meshy/Tripo generation with Blender cleanup (hard-surface shapes survive AI generation far better than foliage) or code-built geometry. Check the generator's plan terms first: free tiers of AI model generators commonly restrict commercial use or ownership; this was not re-verified in this step.

## Record-keeping: what to store with every downloaded asset
Keep one folder per asset and one master list. Suggested layout: a `licenses/` folder in the repository plus `CREDITS.md` and `assets_manifest.csv`.

For each asset, record:
1. Asset name, author/uploader name, and the exact item URL (not the site home page).
2. Licence name and version (e.g. CC0 1.0, CC BY 4.0, Fab Standard) and the URL of the licence text.
3. Date and time of download, and which account was used.
4. Proof of the licence at that moment: a full-page screenshot or saved PDF of the item page showing the licence line, plus an archived copy link (Wayback Machine "Save Page Now"). For Sketchfab also save the item's API record (api.sketchfab.com/v3/models/<id>) as a small JSON file, since it carries the licence field. Licences and listings change or vanish; Sketchfab changed owner in 2026.
5. The original downloaded file, untouched, stored outside the game build (or its SHA-256 hash and file name if it is too large), so the shipped file can be traced to the source.
6. What was changed (decimated, retextured, logos removed, converted to GLB) - CC BY requires noting modifications.
7. The exact credit line to display, copied into `CREDITS.md` and the in-game credits screen. Needed for every CC BY item and for PLATEAU.
8. Any conditions: "no standalone redistribution" (Mixamo, Pixabay, Fab Standard - do not commit these raw to a public repository), trademark or logo clean-up done, and for AI-generated models the tool, plan tier, date and a copy of that plan's terms.
9. Where it is used in the project (file path), so an asset can be pulled quickly if a licence is ever disputed.
10. For Fab/Megascans: the order or library receipt email and a screenshot of the listing's licence field while signed in, since that field did not render for any researcher in this run.

Rule of thumb: if the licence line cannot be seen and captured on the item's own page, do not ship the asset.

## Pages that failed today
- https://www.mlit.go.jp/plateau/site-policy/ - DNS failure (PLATEAU primary licence unverified).
- https://www.blender.org/download/demo-files/ - HTTP 403 (Human Base Meshes CC0 confirmed only via CG Channel and a search snippet).
- https://fonts.google.com/noto/specimen/Noto+Sans+JP/license - returned no content (font licence unverified).
- gdTree3D LICENSE.md not opened (MIT is second-hand).

Nothing was viewed in 3D; all quality judgements are from descriptions and need an eyes-on check.
